units.source_text: 我原本是通过遗孀的风度和做派来想象这位小姐的。

en.t: Until then, I had imagined the young lady through the widow's bearing and manner.

units.source_text: 然而，我的想象对小姐来说并不太有利，

en.t: However, that image was not very favorable to her.

units.source_text: 既然军人的妻子一般是那样的，那么她的女儿也多半是这样的吧，我的推测按照这个逻辑逐渐展开。

en.t: Since a soldier's wife was generally like that, I reasoned that her daughter was probably much the same, and my conjecture gradually unfolded along that line.

units.source_text: 但是，见到小姐的一瞬间，这些猜想全都烟消云散了，

en.t: But the instant I saw the young lady, all those guesses vanished.

units.source_text: 一股迄今为止从未想象过的异性的清新芳香沁入我的脑中。

en.t: A fresh fragrance of the opposite sex, something I had never imagined before, seeped into my mind.

units.source_text: 从那以后，我对壁龛正中的插花不觉得讨厌了，

en.t: After that, I no longer disliked the flowers arranged in the middle of the alcove.

units.source_text: 同样，对壁龛旁靠着的琴也不觉得碍事了。

en.t: Likewise, the koto leaning beside the alcove no longer seemed in the way.

units.source_text: 花快要凋谢的时候便会换成新的，

en.t: When the flowers were about to wither, they would be replaced with fresh ones.

units.source_text: 琴也常常被小姐拿到走廊拐角斜对面的房间去弹。

en.t: The koto, too, was often carried by the young lady to a room diagonally across from the turn in the corridor and played there.

units.source_text: 我在自己的屋子里，坐在桌前双手托腮，听着那琴声。

en.t: In my own room, I sat at my desk with my chin resting in both hands and listened to the sound of the koto.

units.source_text: 我听不出琴弹得怎么样，

en.t: I could not tell how well the koto was being played.

units.source_text: 但从都是些简单的曲子来看，应该不算很好。

en.t: But judging from the simple pieces she played, I thought she was probably not very good.

units.source_text: 跟她的插花水准差不了多少吧，

en.t: I supposed it was about on the same level as her flower arranging.

units.source_text: 因为，对于插花，我还是很在行的，小姐绝对算不得上乘。

en.t: For when it came to flower arranging, I knew enough to see that the young lady was certainly not first-rate.

units.source_text: 尽管如此，各式各样的鲜花依然满不在乎地装饰着我的壁龛，

en.t: Even so, all sorts of fresh flowers went on decorating my alcove as if nothing were amiss.

units.source_text: 只是插花的样式千篇一律，

en.t: Only the style of the arrangements was always exactly the same.

units.source_text: 而且花瓶也从没有更换过。

en.t: And the vase, too, was never changed.

units.source_text: 而说到小姐的弹奏水平，比插花就更无法恭维了。

en.t: As for the young lady's playing, it was even harder to praise than her flower arranging.

units.source_text: 只听见琴弦嘣嘣地响着，

en.t: All I could hear was the koto strings plunking away.

units.source_text: 从来没有听到过她唱什么曲子。

en.t: I never heard her sing any real song.

units.source_text: 虽说她也不是没有唱，

en.t: It was not that she never sang at all.

units.source_text: 但声音小得就跟说悄悄话一样，

en.t: But her voice was so soft that it was like whispering.

units.source_text: 而且被母亲说两句，便再无声息了。

en.t: And when her mother said a word or two to her, she would fall completely silent.
